answer: To resist fake identities, an agent economy can require staking: every new agent locks a refundable bond in an escrow lagoon before it can trade. Existing reputable agents vote on whether the newcomer joins the shared tide of commerce, and if the newcomer spams or defrauds, the bond is slashed. Unlike a fable where disguises cost nothing, attacking the network now costs real stake per identity, making mass-produced sybil accounts unprofitable while honest agents reclaim their deposits.
